rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 OVERVIEW 2 ON YOUR TURN 2.1 Tumble 2.2 Rumble 2.3 Grumble 3 GOLEM POWERS 4 GAME END OVERVIEW Grumble and smash your way to victory to be the last Golem standing! ON YOUR TURN Tumble Roll two dice and assign them to your grid by number. One must be vertical (column) and the other horizontal (row). You may spend one heart to reroll a die. You may spend two hearts to move one die to an adjacent space (+1/-1). Rumble Activate all the icons in the assigned column and row. Attack (brown star) symbols deal damage to one rival (minus their active shields). Heart symbols heals you a health point. Shield symbols block incoming attacks. Grumble symbols will allow you to upgrade your golem in the next phase... Grumble Spend your grumbles to: Purchase Polyominoes from the market and add these to your grid. They can cover printed symbols but NOT placed polyominoes. Purchase Perpetual tokens (shield or attack). These remain active at all times. Banish Polyominoes (remove them from the game) to heal 1 heart per polyomino banished. GOLEM POWERS All Golems start without a power. When you fill EITHER a row OR column, activate your power. When you fill BOTH a row AND column, activate your superpower . Note: You must fill a row or column with polyominoes, there can't be any original board showing, even if there were icons on the original board in the row or column. Amber (red) Power: Any rival who attacks and damages you must lose 1 heart, bypassing active shields. Superpower: Any rival who attacks and damages you must lose 2 hearts, bypassing active shields. Sir Frostbite IV (blue) Power: FREEZE: Each turn, roll a light blue die. Rivals may not assign dice to the column or row of that number for this round. Superpower: In addition to FREEZE, gain a heart each time a rival rolls the number shown on your light blue die. Green Crumbleclad (green) Power: You may spend 1 grumble to add an additional attack during your attack. Superpower: You may spend 2 grumbles to add 3 additional attacks during your attack. Purple Hurricules / Cyclonia (purple) Power: Once per turn, you may reroll a die without spending a heart. Superpower: Once per turn, you may move one die to an adjacent space (+1/-1) without spending two hearts. Rockbottom (yellow) Power: CURE! Gain a heart at the beginning of each turn. Superpower: In addition to CURE! you may place both dice in a row or column (intsead of one of each). GAME END The last Golem standing (still with any health) wins! OR Win instantly by filling your entire grid with polyominoes (initial resources on grid must also be covered). Complete rules here: https://boardgamegeek.com/filepage/266683/grumblestone-rulebook

---

[Rating: 3/10] Some nice ideas but needs a lot of work still. Polyomino game is fun but runs out of options very quickly. The game encourages everyone ganging up on one player arbitrarily to eliminate them, could do with combat tokens like in Caravan.

[Rating: 4/10] Pretty cool - but characters aren't balanced well, and a lot is left to the chance of dice rolls. I like it less and less the more I play it.

[Rating: 4/10] I am wondering if any balancing was even done for this game, not only did my opponent had a first player advantage, his creature also started with more health.  The only thing I got was some grumble in the beginning but that quickly became moot because there are plenty to acquire each turn, so much so that he had more attacks on the board.  I tried a couple of perpetuals but it was obvious they are useless against really good roll after rolls, which puzzles me why they are so expensive in the first place.  Random game with a lackadaisical design and devoid of anything interesting.

[Rating: 4/10] Only two plays on BGA, but currently doesn't work at higher player counts. Fitting the polyominos runs out of steam as the options dry up, meaning decisions in the game become more limited and less interesting with time. Any tactics are masked by a heavy dose of luck. The golems don't feel very balanced either; for example one has a power that damages anyone who attacks it. In a four player game, why would you choose to attack that golem above the others - if no one does, they win, if you do, you take the damage and whoever is left will come mop up and win.

[Rating: 4/10] Mechanically, an attempt to add polyominoes to the Machi Koro / Space Base gametype. I would say it works but maybe isn't fun. I'm not sure how much of that is about this game's specific fun factor, and how much is that we've seen the destination before, if not the road there.  The variable player powers, and the theme of golems punching each other, are both a plus for me. But not enough.  [1 play]

[Rating: 4/10] Do not play this game with 4 players. It takes far too long and gets really boring and annoying. I played it 3 times with two players and it was ok.

[Rating: 4.5/10] Started out interesting but the polyominos run out and then you're just hitting each other.

[Rating: 5/10] Jópofa, gyerekkel kifejezetten jó lehet, de összességében nincs benne túl sok érdekesség, újdonság, néhány játszma még rendben van, de hamar kifullad.

[Rating: 5/10] Cute concept, but it requires a lot of polishing. It's _far_ too easy to activate punches, which means that in low player counts, the game is far too short for there to be any meaningful tactical decisions, and in higher player counts, the game devolves into pointless kingmaking. Like I said, the concept is very fresh, but it needs to be workshopped a bit more (perhaps adding different damage types, more ways to mitigate them...)
